Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral perihilar alveolar consolidations (bat-wing pattern) and pleural effusions, which are classic radiographic signs of acute pulmonary edema secondary to heart failure. While the patient has fever suggesting possible infection, the specific imaging findings described are most characteristic of cardiogenic pulmonary edema rather than pneumonia or other options.
